clue.text: A way to limit supplies is needed in all things so the maxim says

definitions.text: needed in all things so the maxim says

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
to ration is to limit the supplies each person gets

explanation.surface: Rationing is presented as a universal necessity, backed by an old saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The maxim is 'moderation in all things'; the definition is the description of that quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'moderation in all things' recommends restraint everywhere, so restraint is what the saying says is needed.

clue.text: Main ship's timber could be beech, oak, or chestnut

definitions.meaning: the main upright spar of a sailing vessel

definitions.text: could be beech, oak, or chestnut
definitions.meaning: the fallen nuts of forest trees, used as pig food, are called by this word

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's tall spar is one sense; the nuts dropped by beech and oak trees are another.

clue.text: Made free consignment to the door apparently

definitions.meaning: released or rescued
a parcel brought to your doorstep has been handed over

explanation.definitionFit: The word means rescued or set free, and also brought to the doorstep by a courier.

clue.text: One who gets up a steep part of the staircase

definitions.meaning: a person who leaves bed, early or late

definitions.text: a steep part of the staircase
definitions.meaning: the vertical board between two treads of a stair

explanation.definitionFit: An early bird gets out of bed; the upright board of each stair step has the same name.

clue.text: Sailor, one of five children, who rose to be king of Rome

parts.note: tar is a traditional word for a sailor
a quin is one of quintuplets, five born at once

explanation.surface: A seaman born in a set of quintuplets ends up ruling ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarquin was the name of two legendary kings of early Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarquinius Superbus was the last legendary ruler of Rome before the Republic.

clue.text: Ardent lover of Arden

parts.note: points to the hero of Shakespeare's As You Like It, who pins love poems to trees in the Forest of Arden

explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It, the young hero flees to Arden and passionately woos Rosalind there.

clue.text: In the course of confessing to being a bunch of primitive instincts

parts.note: someone confessing to being something says 'I am', giving the verb form am
in Freudian psychology the id is the mind's store of primitive instinctive drives

explanation.surface: Someone owns up, mid-confession, to being driven purely by base urges.
explanation.walkthrough: The ID is Freud's term for the instinctive part of the psyche.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning during or in the middle of something, as 'in the course of' is.

clue.text: Study the art of beer drinking?

definitions.meaning: to cram or swot for an exam
read literally, raising a tankard upwards

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for revising hard; literally it describes lifting your beer tankard.

clue.text: Drastic treatment for hair that is parted, oily, dishevelled

indicators.note: messed-up hair suggests the letters of parted and oily are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A hairdressing disaster: greasy, untidy hair with a parting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair-removing cream or wax is the most extreme thing you can do about unwanted hair.

clue.text: Review twenty four hours in the life of a farmer

definitions.meaning: a military parade or display for inspection

definitions.text: twenty four hours in the life of a farmer
definitions.meaning: literally a day spent out in the fields

explanation.definitionFit: Originally a military display for inspection; literally, a farmer's day out in the meadows.

clue.text: Shilling beers put on to attract bargain hunters

definitions.text: put on to attract bargain hunters

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A pub lays on cheap beer to lure customers looking for a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a British coin worth a twentieth of a pound, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops stage discount events precisely to draw in shoppers hunting for reduced prices.

clue.text: Arriving for the final act of a red-carpet ceremony?

definitions.meaning: to roll up is an informal way to say to turn up or arrive

definitions.text: the final act of a red-carpet ceremony?
definitions.meaning: once the celebrities have gone, the carpet itself is rolled back into a cylinder

explanation.definitionFit: Turning up informally is 'rolling up', and the last job after a premiere is literally furling the carpet away.

clue.text: Upset an open container of brewed tea

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
an urn is a large vessel for keeping tea hot

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a lidless pot of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset something is to knock it over or capsize it.

clue.text: A bit of a flap elegantly tailored

definitions.text: A bit of a flap elegantly tailored

indicators.note: only a part of the words a flap elegantly is taken, the letters running across the join

explanation.surface: A neat piece of fabric folded on a well-cut jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a folded flap on a tailored coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The folded-back flap on the front of a jacket below the collar is exactly this piece of tailoring.

clue.text: Racy types ostentatiously exhibit marks of injury

parts.note: to sport something is to wear or display it proudly
scars are marks left by wounds

explanation.surface: Daring people show off their battle wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racy types' sounds like people, but it means fast models of car.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast two-seater automobiles built for speed are racy models.

clue.text: Not all a bride brings to marriage

definitions.meaning: a part or share of something rather than the whole
a dowry, the property a woman brings to her husband

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a share of a whole, and in older usage also a marriage settlement or dowry.

clue.text: In no danger of being stumped for a pay increment

parts.note: in cricket a batsman behind the crease line cannot be stumped

explanation.surface: A cricketer safe at the wicket asks for a rise.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the line a batsman must be behind; 'stumped' looks like baffled but is a way of being out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in salary is a growth in one's pay.

clue.text: Maybe Ostia supplies vintage wine

definitions.meaning: Ostia was the ancient harbour town of Rome, an example of a former harbour
a long-aged fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.definitionFit: Ostia is an ancient harbour city, and aged fortified Douro wine matured for years is the same phrase.

clue.text: So Lourdes contrived to be free of atmospheric pollution

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so the letters of So Lourdes are rearranged

explanation.surface: The pilgrimage town of Lourdes engineered to have clean air.
explanation.definitionFit: Air with no smell has no stink or fumes in it, so it is unpolluted.

clue.text: The root of Liberalism

parts.note: the word for a root (from Latin radix) is also the name of the reforming movement from which the Liberal party grew

explanation.definitionFit: The word derives from Latin for root, and nineteenth-century reformers so called formed the basis of British Liberalism.

clue.text: Sort of English verse celebrated in th century Vatican

definitions.meaning: verse with internal rhyme between the middle and end of a line
the walled district of Rome built by Pope Leo IV in the ninth century bears this name

explanation.walkthrough: The printed '9th' has lost its numeral; the Leonine City around the Vatican was walled by Leo IV in the 840s.
explanation.definitionFit: Internally rhyming verse takes the name, as does the walled papal district named after Pope Leo.

clue.text: It sounds like a detour is needed for a coach excursion

indicators.note: signals that the spoken form of the next word gives the answer

parts.note: a detour is a roundabout route, said here to match the answer's sound

explanation.surface: A tour bus has to take a diversion on its outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-day sightseeing trip by bus is a classic coach outing.

clue.text: What campers erected in current state of international harmony

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as the campers' shelter goes inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river, a flowing current
campers put up a tent

explanation.surface: Campers pitch their shelter in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The DEE is a British river; 'current' is the flowing water.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for relaxation describes a thaw in tense relations between nations.

clue.text: No real point feeling it if you are not to blame

definitions.text: No real point feeling it if you are not to blame

parts.note: a sham is something not real, a fake
E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: Reassurance that guilt is pointless when something is not your fault.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as advice in which the answer fills the gap after 'feeling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilt or embarrassment over wrongdoing is pointless when you did nothing wrong.

clue.text: Commercial designer is a chap of the present era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels years of the present era
a man is a chap

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who creates advertisements works in commercials.

clue.text: The open air cannot possibly lead to…

parts.note: something that is out is not an option and cannot possibly happen
doors are what lead to entry, continuing into the next clue

explanation.surface: A sentence about being outside that runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 27 across: doors lead to admission.
explanation.definitionFit: Being outside, beyond buildings, is being in the open air.

clue.text: Should be commonly used for anything or nothing

definitions.meaning: a modal verb of obligation

definitions.text: be commonly used for anything or nothing
definitions.meaning: in popular use the word stands for aught (anything) or naught (nothing, zero)

explanation.definitionFit: The modal of duty matches 'should'; colloquially it also stands for aught or nought.

clue.text: They may be used for writing on shrivelled skin

definitions.text: They may be used for writing

indicators.note: shrivelled skin is wrinkled out of shape, so the letters of skin are rearranged

explanation.surface: Writing on wrinkled skin, perhaps a tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured fluids for pens are what writing is done with.

clue.text: … a confession

parts.note: continues the previous clue: doors lead to entry, and the same word means owning up

explanation.definitionFit: Owning up to something is making an avowal of it, and entry through doors is the other sense.

clue.text: Inexperienced as an environmentalist

definitions.meaning: naive and new to something
describes someone campaigning for ecological causes

explanation.definitionFit: The colour word means raw and untried, and also ecologically minded, as in the political party.

clue.text: In this way Poles produce children

parts.note: so means in this way or thus
N is the north pole
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: A remark on how Polish people have offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the people of Poland, but it gives the two magnetic poles, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Male offspring are children.

clue.text: Desist! Fate shatters! That is their advice

indicators.note: breaking into pieces signals the letters of desist and fate are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doom-laden cries: stop, destiny is breaking everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desist!' is the advice pessimists give, which the clue's last words point back to.
explanation.definitionFit: Pessimists who expect to lose counsel giving up, so 'desist' is their typical advice.
